methods.label: Connect the center to the tangency points
methods.explanation:
A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent, so connecting the circle's center to \(A\) and \(D\) will turn the arc question into an angle question. First draw diagonal \(AD\). Each interior angle of the regular pentagon is
\[
\frac{(5-2)180^\circ}{5}=108^\circ.
\]
Since \(EA=ED\), triangle \(EAD\) is isosceles, with vertex angle \(AED=108^\circ\). Thus
\[
\angle EAD=\frac{180^\circ-108^\circ}{2}=36^\circ,
\qquad
\angle BAD=108^\circ-36^\circ=72^\circ.
\]
Let \(O\) be the circle's center. Because \(AB\) is tangent at \(A\), \(OA\perp AB\). The center is on the same side of this tangent as the other circle point \(D\), so
\[
\angle OAD=90^\circ-72^\circ=18^\circ.
\]
The radii \(OA\) and \(OD\) are equal, so triangle \(AOD\) has equal base angles of \(18^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle AOD=180^\circ-2(18^\circ)=144^\circ.
\]
An arc's degree measure equals its central angle. Since \(144^\circ<180^\circ\), the minor arc \(AD\) measures \(\boxed{144^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
